title: The North Face Wawona 4 review: a stand-up car-camping tent for two plus a kid
dek: Tall, airy and easy to pitch, with a front porch big enough for camp chairs. It's comfortable for two adults and a child, tight for four adults, and happiest in fair to moderate weather.
subject: The North Face Wawona 4
verdict: The Wawona 4 is a roomy, well-ventilated car-camping tent that you can stand up in, with the most useful vestibule in its class. Buy it for couples, a couple with a kid, or anyone who hates crawling around a dome tent. Look elsewhere if you camp on exposed ridges, in shoulder-season cold, or with four adults who all want elbow room.
bestFor: Two adults plus a child or a dog, car camping and festival weekends, campers who want to stand up and keep chairs out of the rain.
notFor: Four adults with full-width pads, backpacking, high-wind exposed sites, cold nights below about 40°F.
pros: 75-inch peak height lets most adults stand up near the door
27.6 sq ft front vestibule works as a covered porch for chairs and gear

Freestanding with color-coded DAC MX poles, so setup is straightforward
Plenty of interior pockets and ceiling storage
cons: Partial-coverage fly and tall profile give up storm protection in strong wind
Lots of mesh makes it drafty on cold nights

13 lb packed, so it's strictly a car-camping tent

body:
## The short version

The Wawona 4 is built around one idea: a tent you can live in, not just sleep in. An arched front pole lifts the peak to 75 inches, so most adults can stand near the door, and the front vestibule is big enough to set up two camp chairs out of the rain. For a couple, or a couple with a kid, that's a big step up from a typical dome tent.

The trade-offs come from the same design choices. A tall tent with a partial fly catches more wind and lets in more cold air than a squat dome with a full fly. It's a fair-weather-to-moderate-weather car-camping tent, and it's very good at that job.

## Space: who actually fits

The floor is 96 by 90 inches, about 58 square feet. Here's what that means with real sleeping pads:

- **Two adults:** plenty of room, with space along the walls for bags and a walkway to the door.
- **Two adults and a child (or a big dog):** the sweet spot. Everyone fits without touching.
- **Four adults:** four standard 20-inch-wide pads take up 80 of the 90 inches of width. It works for a night, but there's no room for gear inside and everyone climbs over each other to reach the doors.

If you regularly camp with four adults, step up to the Wawona 6. If you need to stand up fully and you're over six feet, measure against the 75-inch peak: it's tallest only along the arched door pole and drops toward the back wall.

## The vestibule is the reason to buy it

The front vestibule covers 27.6 square feet, roughly half the area of the tent floor. With the door panel rolled back it becomes a covered porch: chairs, a cooler, boots and packs all stay dry, and you can sit outside during an afternoon thunderstorm without being cooped up inside. The rear vestibule adds another 14.9 square feet, which is about right for duffels and shoes.

Add the floor and both vestibules together and you have just over 100 square feet of covered space, which is what makes the Wawona feel bigger than its floor number.

## Setup

The Wawona 4 is freestanding, with three DAC MX aluminum poles. Poles and clips are color-coded to their sleeves and corners, so there's little guesswork. Two people can pitch it in about 10 to 15 minutes once they've done it once. The tall door pole is easiest with a second set of hands.

Stake out the vestibules and every guyline. The tent stands without stakes, but the vestibule only works as a porch when it's staked taut.

## Rain, wind and cold

The canopy and fly are 75-denier polyester with a 1,200 mm polyurethane coating. That's a typical rating for car-camping tents: fine for summer storms and steady rain when the tent is pitched tight, but not a storm-shelter rating.

The fly doesn't cover the whole tent. That's great for airflow and for stargazing, and independent testers stayed dry in light to moderate rain. The downside is in strong wind: the tall profile and partial fly make it noisier and less stable than a lower dome. On Colorado's exposed sites, pitch it with the narrow end into the wind, use every guyline, and look for some shelter from trees.

The large mesh door and walls also mean it's drafty when temperatures drop. It's comfortable through a normal three-season range, but on near-freezing nights you'll feel the air moving and want a warmer bag.

## Ventilation and condensation

This is where the mesh pays off. The big mesh front door and two roof vents move a lot of air, so condensation stays low even with four people breathing inside. Rolling up the fly panels opens large windows for more airflow on hot nights. The one annoyance: adjusting those panels means stepping outside.

## Durability

The DAC MX poles and the stitching are good quality. The weak spot, according to owner reviews, is the floor: a couple of owners report holes or seepage through the floor. A footprint fixes most of that. It's sold separately, and on gravel or rocky campgrounds it's worth it.

A few owners also report snapping a pole section and struggling to get a single replacement section from the manufacturer. If that happens to you, search your tent model in our [replacement pole finder](/poles).

## Weight and packing

At 13 pounds packed and 24 by 9 inches, this is a trunk tent, not a backpacking tent. It carries fine from the car to the site in its duffel-style bag with carry straps.

## Which Wawona 4 do you have?

The Wawona 4 has been updated over the years. Older versions are listed with a 68-inch peak and a slightly smaller 95 by 87 inch floor. The current version is listed at 75 inches and 96 by 90 inches. If you're comparing listings or buying replacement parts, check the product tag on the tent body or the stuff sack for the style number. The current version's style number is NF0A8BDU.

## Wawona 4 or Wawona 6?

Choose the Wawona 4 for two adults with a kid or dog, or if you want the smaller, lighter package. Choose the Wawona 6 for three or more adults, more standing room and a bigger vestibule.

## Bottom line

The Wawona 4 is one of the most livable car-camping tents for its size. It's tall, airy, easy to pitch, and the front porch changes how you camp in bad weather. Treat it as a fair-to-moderate-weather tent, put a footprint under it, and it's an easy recommendation for couples and small families.
